The Helan Mountains, sometimes referred to as a “mountain island in the sky,” form a barrier separating the semi-arid Ordos Plateau and Yellow River Valley from the desert regions of the Alxa Plateau to the west. Similar to the mountain ranges in western North America’s Great Basin, the Helan Range isolates dense conifer forests and may support unique, endemic communities of flora and fauna. Although this ecoregion has received insufficient scientific attention, it is home to several rare species, including blue sheep, blue-eared pheasants, and the endemic Helan pika. Commercial logging remains a threat, continuing to cause habitat destruction and jeopardizing the region’s high biological diversity.

We aim to reduce costs even further by developing an ultra-high efficiency InGaN solar cell. [2] The band gap can be tuned between 0.7eV and 3.4eV by changing the ratio of indium to gallium in the film. This allows for a multi-layered structure which will capture the entire solar spectrum. As a result, a well designed InGaN solar cell will convert a much higher percentage of the sun's light energy into electricity. Our research will proceed in two stages. The first stage will be the characterization and basic understanding of InGaN as a semiconducting material. The final stage will use the information gathered to determine the optimal number of layers and relative concentrations of indium and gallium in each to maximize light absorption and ultimately electricity generation.

In C. tripartitum, animals showed an overall avoidance of less than 10% after the first few positive trials, suggesting that this species adapts to the nose-touch stimulus faster than C. elegans and the others (Figure 5A). However, during the first three trials, C. tripartitum showed a quantitatively similar response to C. elegans (Figure S2 in Additional file 2). Ablation of ASH neurons in five nose-touch responsive species resulted in the loss of nose-touch avoidance (Figure 5A). Although four of five species still showed some nose-touch responses in 20–30% of trials (Figure 5A), Caenorhabditis sp. 3 was unique in that its ASH-ablated animals completely lacked the ability to respond to nose touch (Figure 5A). Ablation of the AWC neuron did not affect the response to nose touch in the different species (Figure S3 in Additional file 2).

Alitrunk (Fig. 15) conspicuously swollen, at a much higher level than propodeal dorsum. Propodeum armed with a pair of strong spines which are straight to slightly upcurved. Metanotal groove absent. Metapleural lobes triangular, conspicuous. Petiole in profile with elongate peduncle and with well-developed node, the dorsum of which slopes down posteriorly so that the posterior face is short. Anterior and dorsal surfaces of postpetiole forming a single convexity, posterior face truncated. In dorsal view the nodes of both petiole and postpetiole broader than long. Dorsum of head strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5-7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye-level. These rugae are irregular and tend to meander slightly, a few anastomoses usually present. Scrobal area largely smooth but usually with 1-2 fine rugulae traversing its width just behind the antennal fossa. Sides of head behind the eyes finely reticulate-rugose, this sculpture extending around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. All spaces between the rugae unsculptured, or at most with the faintest superficial traces. Dorsal alitrunk everywhere finely but strongly reticulate-rugose, with broad shining interspaces. Petiole dorsum rugulose, postpetiole varying from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. Gaster unsculptured. All dorsal surfaces of head and body densely clothed with fine acute hairs. Colour dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

Counter moves known as Repels are now a special move that stuns the opponent and leaves them vulnerable to a subsequent counterattack. To perform a Repel, the player must press + to counter high-level attacks, including special and super moves, or + to counter low attacks. After a successful Repel, the player must press again to counterattack the opponent. Kaede and Akari can perform Repels in mid-air, which knocks down the opponent without inflicting any damage. These air Repels are effective against special moves, whether they are performed on the ground or in mid-air.

Takamatsu is very famous in Japan for its udon, one of Japan's three major noodle types. Takamatsu udon noodles are white, fairly thick and chewy. The kind produced in Kagawa Prefecture is sometimes called "Sanuki udon" (Sanuki being the pre-modern name for Kagawa), but this kind of udon is so popular in Japan that it is often considered to be the "normal" udon. In fact, when most Japanese people hear the word "udon" they think of the Takamatsu variety. Udon is available all over Japan, but Takamatsu does it better and cheaper than anywhere else. There are literally hundreds of udon shops within the city limits. As local foods are a major draw for Japanese tourists, many people visit Takamatsu for the udon, and some go on "chain-eating" tours to visit the most famous shops.

However, Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) cannot be used to substantiate claims of carbon neutrality for electrical use beyond a claimant's metered use of electricity because most RECs are derived from projects that would have been financially viable without the sale of RECs. [10] They do not have the essential attribute of additionality. Additionality refers to the counterfactual, or what would have happened in the absence of the purchase or contract of a REC. There are many different frameworks for testing additionality, but the essential question is whether the project would have survived financially without the revenue from REC sales. Without proof of additionality, RECs are not equivalent to emissions offsets.

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation, based on the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975). From this equation, we obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over uneven bottom. It is shown that by using only linear dispersion for steady waves, the equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), which is called the modified mild-slope equation (MMSE), can be obtained. To the leading-order solution, it is found that the modified curvature terms of the MMSE have significant effects, while the slope square terms are negligible according to the mild-slope assumption. Therefore, we kept all the modified curvature terms neglected in the MSE, and developed a uniform model. A numerical model based on the finite element method (FEM) is developed to predict wave scattering by a varying bottom. In general, the uniform model can predict salient features of waves over various sea beds, such as sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, the results of the uniform model are in closer agreement with experimental data than other established models. For man-made bars, the results of both the MMSE and the uniform model are in closer agreement with experimental data than the results of Kirby (1986). An important result of the FEM model is its application to the transformation of waves over arbitrarily-varying bathymetry.

The world was once a place where reality and myth mixed together, and it was only with the development of modern comparative biology that the distinction between the two became clear. But science has not abolished the liminal zone in which a figure like Buraq dwells. We need such transitional objects to connect seemingly divergent realms of empirical knowledge and spiritual experience. Her presence in contemporary culture serves as a bridge between rationalist taxonomies and the vestigial power of myth. This is nowhere more forcefully expressed than in the Islamic transport industry, where Buraq, a figure combining piety and speed, recurs as a patron saint. She gives her name to airlines from Libya to Indonesia, bus companies, freight ships, motorcycle taxis, a space camp, an engineering college, and Pakistan’s first drone. The fluidity of Buraq as an aesthetic and linguistic object explains her pliability in commercial use: she presides not just over wings and wheels, but is also used to sell plastic and PVC, heavy metal and heavy-duty diesel (BURAQ LUBRICANTS), Indian food, and surgical instruments.

When London’s King’s Cross station expanded north in the mid-1860s, its tracks cut through St. Pancras Old Church, the city’s oldest site of Christian worship. Thomas Hardy, then working as an architect, was called in to clear the land. Hardy exhumed the dead and arranged their gravestones in a spiral around a central tree. That tree still stands today, its roots slowly enveloping the stones, making the inscriptions harder and harder to read. Elsewhere in the cemetery, monuments mark the graves of other notables, including Mary Wollstonecraft, author of A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792) and mother of Mary Shelley, author of Frankenstein (1818). Nearby is an imposing mausoleum bearing the name Sir John Soane, the collector-architect whose eccentric house is still standing on Lincoln’s Inn Fields (see Description of the House and Museum of Sir John Soane, 1835).

Social media is currently abuzz with videos of alleged queues of dead bodies waiting to be cremated outside crematoriums in Maharashtra. The visuals, which can be seen here and here, are being circulated amid a recent surge in COVID-19 cases in India. India Today Anti Fake News Wing fact-checked the claim and found it to be misleading. The claim: Visuals show dead bodies waiting to be cremated outside crematoriums in Maharashtra. Fact: The visuals were actually shot recently at a cemetery in Surat, Gujarat. The video shows a long line of dead bodies of COVID-19 victims waiting for cremation at the Umra Crematorium in Surat and has no connection with Maharashtra. Conclusion: The claim is false.

The myth in the Phaedrus is of a far higher kind than the preceding, and also more distinctly Platonism. It is an ascent not to the future, but to the former existence of men. Reason is represented strug-gling with the animal nature, which is aided by passion or righteous indignation; the charioteer and the steeds of the soul. Man has existed before in the company of some god, and seen truth in the universal or ideal form; he is now seeking to return to the former state. Or rather the world below is the former world, and we are always going from one to the other. The religious mystic in whom the contemplative and emotional elements predominate, would naturally see the world under this aspect of reverie. The language of the Phaedrus throws a degree of haze over the subject, which prevents us from perceiving distinctly that in this as in the other myths the future is a figure of speech transferred to the past, and that the question really is, What is the existence of men in the world before birth or after death? Is there a better question or one of more concern to us, than this? Yet we remark that to Plato himself the difference between the two is comparatively slight. For he is very willing to see in the one a description of the eternal world, in which he places the realities of things, in the other a picture of the future life. William Cowper was 61 when he wrote this ballad. But the road to those words was a descent through despair. This ecoregion represents the moist deciduous forests surrounding the montane rainforests of the northern portion of the Western Ghats. This ecoregion extends across the states of Maharashtra and Karnataka in western India. Gondwana is the origin of this region, and during the Cretaceous period, the Deccan Plate detached from Gondwanaland, drifted north, and reattached with the northern Eurasian continent. Later geological uplift formed the Western Ghats Mountains, which intercepted the southwestern monsoon rains and created a moisture gradient from wet on the windward side to increasingly dry on the leeward side. The annual rainfall in this ecoregion ranges from 1,500 to 2,000 mm and is followed by a 4 to 5-month dry season. Although the mean annual temperature ranges from 24 to 27oC, inland maximum temperatures can be quite high, exceeding 40oC.

Human beings develop spoken language within the first few years of life, and hearing impairment can not only prevent the ability to hear but also to understand spoken language. Deaf children who are not provided with a sign language (instead of a spoken language) during their early years will likely develop language deprivation and may not achieve good psychosocial skills or mental abilities. By the time it is noticed that a severely hearing impaired (deaf) child has a hearing deficit, problems with communication may have already caused issues within the family and hindered social skills, unless the child is part of a Deaf community where sign language is used instead of spoken language (see Deaf Culture). In many developed countries, hearing is evaluated during the newborn period in an effort to prevent the inadvertent isolation of a deaf child in a hearing family. Although sign language is a full means of communication, literacy depends on understanding speech. In the great majority of written language, the sound of the word is coded in symbols. Although an individual who hears and learns spoken language and then becomes deaf with age can understand written language, an individual who never heard well enough to learn to speak is rarely able to read proficiently (see [4]). Most evidence indicates that a child with very insensitive hearing has to learn spoken language if he or she is to learn to read and write. Listening is important in learning a second language.

That mode of treating elegant manners put them out of fashion; they were speedily abandoned, and the barbarity of their successors still so lingers amongst us, that every day you see put into the lumber-room an elegant Grecian chair which has broken your arm, and canopies which smell of the stable, because they are stuffed with hay.

All of de Sève's illustrations are equipped with identifying captions except one, listed simply as l'animal anonyme (the unidentified animal). Most later naturalists agreed it must be meant to represent a fennec fox, though some have also suggested a bat-eared fox. Whatever the case may be, one thing is certain: de Sève loved drawing large ears. With their strangely human faces and richness of setting, De Sève's wonderful illustrations, engraved for publication in the Histoire by Louis Le Grand, are a true treasure of eighteenth-century naturalism. In the nervous system, transduction is the conversion of stimuli into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, physical or chemical stimuli are converted by sensory receptors into electrical impulses that are sent to the brain. In the visual system, rod and cone cells in the retina transduce light into electrical signals. When light hits the photoreceptor, it causes a conformational change in the protein rhodopsin. This change initiates a cascade of events that alters the electrochemical gradient of the photoreceptor. This decrease in the electrochemical gradient causes a decrease in the electrical signals sent to the brain. Thus, more light hitting the photoreceptor results in fewer electrical impulses being sent to the brain.

The strange little animal lights a lamp at the end of its tail to celebrate the joys of life, and everybody knows it by name, even if it is seldom seen roaming through the grass like a spark fallen from the full moon. The Greeks of old called it the Bright-tailed, and modern science names it Lampyris. Mobile internet expands the immersive potential of storytelling by introducing electronic games powered by portable, location-aware interfaces. This latest iteration in the evolution of electronic games seeks to empower the player not only as an avatar in a gameworld, but also as a co-author alongside original designers. Location-aware interfaces allow players to implicate places in the physical world as part of their gameworld and vice versa, a first for interactive media. Beyond empowering the player in worldmaking, mobile games eschew linear narratives in favor of cooperative storytelling reliant on the player's experience of place. While this "author-player" worldmaking concept is not new, mobile games evolve the process beyond traditional video game constraints. By extending the worldmaking process beyond the screen and into the physical world, location-aware interfaces co-opt the player's sensory experiences of real-world places as storytelling tools. In this essay, we theorize the unique storytelling potential of mobile games while describing our experience attempting to harness this potential through the design and implementation of our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.

The House of Representatives on Thursday, in a historic and unanimous vote, rejected a motion seeking to integrate the Almajiri education system into the Universal Basic Education, UBE, programme. This package contains datasets, constants, conversion factors and utilities for use in Marine, Riverine, Estuarine, LAcustrine and COastal science. The package contains: (1) chemical and physical constants and datasets, e.g. atomic weights, gas constants, the earth's bathymetry; (2) conversion factors, e.g. from gram to mole to volume, from barometric to depth, temperature, salinity; (3) physical functions, e.g. to estimate concentration or density of conservative substances, gas transfer, diffusion coefficients, the Coriolis force and gravity; (4) thermophysical properties of the seawater, as from the UNESCO polynomial or from the more recent derivation based on the Gibbs function.

The total volume of lung tissue was calculated as volume of lung tissue = number of voxels × volume of the voxel, provided the compartment considered has a CT number above zero. The change in functional residual capacity resulting from PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) was computed as the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between PEEP and ZEEP. Alveolar derecruitment was defined as the difference in gas volume in poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between PEEP and ZEEP. We also computed the changes in gas volume from PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated lung regions, which were characterized by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2). As previously described [21], the distribution of lost lung aeration for each patient (lung morphology) was classified as diffuse, patchy, and lobar based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.

The Ruhr Area (German Ruhrgebiet) or, simply, Ruhr, is an urban area in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany consisting of a number of large formerly industrial cities, including Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna and Witten. The region has about five million inhabitants and is larger than Berlin, Hamburg or Munich. The Ruhr Area is full of motorways, but hitchhiking is quite hard because of the many minor roads. The main motorways are A1, A2 and A3. If you want to hitch here, you should stay on these motorways. It's really hard to hitch on the minor roads as there is almost no transit traffic. Germany is a nice place to hitch, but the Ruhr Area is the worst part of the country from this point of view. Hitching inside the Ruhr Area can be compared to hitching in a big city like Istanbul. The cities are independent, but for a traveler they all seem like districts of one big city.
